speaker_notes: Two voices. The service host/announcer identifies himself at 0:14:35: "If I haven't met you yet, I'm Pastor Kevin" — he does the announcements, the closing remarks (1:24:56) and the benediction, but he does NOT preach. The preacher is a different man who takes the platform at 0:43:23 ("man getting Pentecostal already, okay, that's great"). He refers to Pastor Kevin in the third person as the previous week's preacher (0:45:02 "Last message in 1 Thessalonians chapter 5 verses 16-22, Pastor Kevin left us with some bite-sized chunks"), names his wife twice ("Cindy's car" 0:46:03; "Cindy's out of town" 0:59:48), speaks of "the life of a pastor, against the life of me" (0:59:27), and in his closing prayer quotes God addressing him by name: "I know you said to me even about this, 'Watch me work, Pat. Watch me work'" (1:15:13) — so the preacher is Pastor Pat. Audience cues are strongly local and interactive: call-and-response ("Say that with me" 0:44:15; "Now, let's say it out loud. God is for me" 1:05:20), a show-of-hands moment, Tucson references (a photo taken driving "from Phoenix through Eloy" in monsoon rain, 0:46:41), the church's "big mess" back-to-school event, and "God is for our church" (1:06:31).
boundary_note: The worship set and the worship leader's prayer end at 0:43:16 with the congregational "amen" at 0:43:20. The preacher's first words are at 0:43:23 ("man getting Pentecostal already okay that's great, I'm a little bit loud on the mic"), immediately followed by "open your Bibles to 1 Thessalonians 5" (0:43:33) and his reading of 5:23-24, so the opening banter plus the scripture reading are counted as the start of the sermon proper. He says "Let's pray" at 1:14:22; the closing pastoral prayer runs to its last words "So I'm watching, Lord" at 1:15:20, after which the band re-enters at 1:15:54 with "Worthy is the Lamb." Everything before 0:43:23 (four worship songs, announcements about the "big mess" event, offering prayer) and everything after 1:15:20 (three songs, Pastor Kevin's closing remarks and benediction, exit music) is service, not sermon.
passage: 1 Thessalonians 5:23-24, expounded almost entirely through Romans 8:1, 31-35 (with Romans 4:23-25, 5:1, 7:24, Philippians 1:6 and 1 John 3:2 brought in)

attribution.notes: The preacher never names Alistair Begg, Truth For Life, or any sermon he consulted. Not once does he use a borrowing signal such as "I read," "one preacher said," "as someone has put it," or "I'm indebted to." Everything is delivered in his own first person, including material that is Begg's own first-person testimony: at 0:56:23 he says "And that's been true this week. At least for me, it's been very true this week that I haven't done all the good that I long to do" — Begg's line is "And that's been true this week. It has for me. I have not lived and done all the good for which I longed." The only citations he does give (Westminster Confession, Zinzendorf, Phillips, "Jer"/Packer) are precisely the four secondary sources Begg cites, cited at the same points in the same argument, which suggests the citations themselves came from Begg rather than from independent reading. Note also that at 0:52:45 he attributes to "1 Thessalonians 5:4" a sentence that is actually Begg's own summary ("the experience of all real Christians, everyone and at all times"), i.e. Begg's commentary has been mistaken for the text.

Point 1: 'blameless at his coming' — the word Paul uses only here; Thessalonian tombstones; the day of completion; 1 John 3:2; Philippians 1:6; Zinzendorf's hymn; the 'what/how question'; verse 24 as the answer; Phillips' rendering; God is not the author of unfinished business (0:47:01-0:53:28)

Point 2: reckon God's faithfulness in the face of accusation — Westminster Confession's 'continual irreconcilable war'; 'that's been true this week'; Romans 7:24; Pogo, 'we have met the enemy and he is us'; Romans 8:1; the onslaught of hell; the flat-tire story; Packer's list of troubled Christians; where do I ground my assurance; feelings vs theology; Johnny Cochran / Robert Shapiro; 'If God is for us'; 'God is for me'; God's decision to justify cannot be altered; sleeping like a baby; McCain joke; 'you don't understand me the way God understands me'; don't let the enemy drag you back into the garbage can (0:55:24-1:10:39)
Point 3: reflect on God's faithfulness in the light of the provision of his son — Romans 8:32; the bicycle with no pedals (1:10:22-1:11:48)
Point 4: behold God's faithfulness expressed in the love of Christ — Romans 8:35, 38; why do we still believe? God's faithfulness (1:11:48-1:12:50)

outline_begg: Continuing from the morning message; the last two of four points on 1 Thess 5:23-24: the product that emerges from the process, and the promise by which he assures them

The product: 'kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ' — the only occasion Paul employs this word; Thessalonican tombstones bearing 'holoclerus'; cross-reference to 3:13; a day of entirety and completeness; 1 John 3:2; 'in the present we are under construction'; Philippians 1:6; Zinzendorf's hymn ('bold shall I stand'; 'this spotless robe'); the 'what question, the how question, the can it possibly be question'
The promise (v24): 'the one who calls you is faithful and he will do it' — or in Phillips, 'utterly faithful ... will finish what he has set out to do'; God is not the author of unfinished business

Turn to Romans 8 to expound it: no condemnation (v1) to no separation (v39); the progression of Romans 1-5; the Westminster Confession's 'continual and irreconcilable war'; 'that's been true this week ... it has for me'; Romans 7:24; Romans 8:1

All-round righteousness meets all-round pressure; the total onslaught of hell; Packer's list of troubled Christians; 'how then am I to cope? Where may I turn? ... the answer is in the faithfulness of God'; evangelical thinking correcting emotional thinking
Four sub-points from Romans 8: (a) v31 God is for us — 'one of the great four words statements'; personalise it: 'God is for me'
(b) v32 God's faithfulness in the giving of his Son; Psalm 84:11

(c) v33 God's faithfulness in the face of accusation — God decided to justify you and knew everything; nobody can produce new evidence of your depravity; 'this is the way to sleep like a baby at night'; 'you don't understand me the way God understands me'; don't let the devil drag you back to the garbage cans; Augustus Toplady's hymn

(d) v35 God's faithfulness expressed in the love of Christ; the dandelion 'he loves me, he loves me not'; 1 Peter 1:5; 'you are not strong enough to fall away while God is resolved to hold you'; Romans 8:38-39
Close: 'carve it into your recollection as you begin tomorrow morning ... God is for me'; Toplady, 'the work which his goodness began'; 'Take my life and let it be'
outline_comparison: Same skeleton, lightly reordered and re-verbed. Both men take 1 Thessalonians 5:23-24, work the identical sequence inside it (the rare word 'blameless at his coming' and the Thessalonian tombstones, 1 John 3:2, Philippians 1:6, Zinzendorf's two hymn stanzas, the 'what/how question', verse 24 answered in the Phillips translation, 'God is not the author of unfinished business'), then make the same pivot — 'how can we be sure of this? Turn to this great chapter,' Romans 8 — and run the same 'no condemnation to no separation' frame, the same Romans 1-5 recap, the same Westminster Confession line, the same Packer list, and the same four sub-points drawn from Romans 8:31, 32, 33, 35. The only structural change is that FBC promotes Begg's four Romans 8 sub-points into the sermon's headline outline announced at 0:44:02, swaps the order of provision (v32) and accusation (v33), and replaces Begg's fourfold repeated verb 'consider' with an alliterative-ish consider / reckon / reflect / behold. Begg's Toplady material, his Psalm 84:11, his dandelion illustration and his 1 Peter section are dropped; FBC substitutes his own illustrations in those slots.

paraphrase_examples.begg: If you get nothing else out of today, get that little phrase from verse 31 and carve it into your recollection as you begin tomorrow morning ... say this to yourself, well I know one thing for sure, God is for me.
paraphrase_examples.comment: The final take-home line of both sermons, same verb ('carve'), same phrase, same placement. Borrowing the conclusion is stronger evidence than borrowing the middle.

original_material.summary: The FBC preacher supplies his own opening (a run of 'daily grind' images and a personal photograph), his own illustrations in most of the slots where Begg had illustrations, congregational interaction, and his own closing prayer. Crucially, ALL of his substitutions sit inside Begg's frame: they decorate Begg's points, they never generate a point. Where Begg has Augustus Toplady's hymn twice, the dandelion 'he loves me, he loves me not', Psalm 84:11, 1 Peter 1:5 and the Packer aphorism 'you are not strong enough to fall away while God is resolved to hold you', FBC substitutes Pogo, a flat bicycle tyre, O.J. Simpson's defence team, John McCain on the Tonight Show, a bicycle without pedals, and 'Let's get ready to rumble'. He also adds a few genuinely his own theological touches — 'There's a difference between being innocent and blameless', the 'just as if I'd never sinned' wordplay on justification, the extra step of contrasting feelings AND logic with theology (Begg contrasts only emotional with evangelical thinking), and an actual quotation of 1 John 3:2 where Begg only paraphrases it. The exegesis, the argument, the sequence, the secondary citations and the conclusion are Begg's.
examples: The 'daily grind' image set — chewed homework, 'a battlefield', 'I just survived taking Cindy's car in to find out the transmission is broke', shadows scattering light, an anchor tethering one firm in a storm (0:45:53-0:46:35)

A personal photograph: 'Rain crowned by a rainbow. A couple weeks ago, I took this picture. I was driving from Phoenix through Eloy during one of these monsoons that we've been having' (0:46:35-0:47:01) — local Tucson colour, entirely his own

Walt Kelly's Pogo: 'On April 22nd, 1971, a cartoonist by the name of Walt Kelly had a character named Pogo ... We have met the enemy and he is us' (0:56:57-0:57:34), with his own turn 'the first enemy that you have to deal with is neither someone else or even the devil itself ... It's you'
The flat-tyre-and-lost-phone story: 'I got on a bicycle Saturday to ride and within five minutes I had a flat tire ... it isn't about falling. It's about getting up' (0:59:46-1:00:32)

The O.J. Simpson defence-team riff: 'God is our Johnny Cochran. God is our Robert Shapiro ... Do you need Johnny Cochran to say if it don't fit it must have quit?' (1:03:54-1:04:26) — congregational Q&A, distinctively American, no counterpart in Begg
The John McCain / Jay Leno 'I slept like a baby' joke (1:08:36-1:08:53), grafted onto Begg's borrowed 'sleep like a baby' line

The bicycle-with-no-pedals illustration for Romans 8:32: 'It's a great bike, but there's no pedals. Well, Dad, where's the pedals? ... He's going to give you the pedals' (1:10:42-1:11:41) — replaces Begg's Psalm 84:11

Wordplay: 'like that announcer before the big wrestling matches. Let's get ready to rumble. Well, let's get ready to reckon' (1:10:07-1:10:22); and 'We're justified in Christ. It's just as if I'd never sinned' (1:02:46)
'There's a difference between being innocent and blameless' (1:05:43) — his own distinction, not in Begg

Local/congregational application: 'God is for our church' (1:06:31), the mechanic exchange 'if a broken transmission is the worst thing that happens to me, man, I'm a blessed person' (1:13:55), and the closing prayer naming his own besetting sin of judging others and 'Watch me work, Pat' (1:14:22-1:15:20)

personalisation_patterns: Begg's evening service becomes a Sunday morning: 'it is true tonight concerning you' becomes 'It's true for you this morning' (1:04:58); 'Tonight we face animosity' becomes 'So what's going on today? Today we might face animosity' (1:05:55).

Begg's British idiom is Americanised: 'garbage cans of sins' stays but 'the devil' becomes 'the enemy' (1:09:49); 'brighten up ... shape up ... shut up' becomes 'time to brighten it up. Time to shape up ... time to shut up' (1:07:34).

Begg's single repeated verb 'consider' across four Romans 8 sub-points is varied into a preachable quartet — consider / reckon / reflect / behold — and promoted to the sermon's announced outline (0:44:02).

Begg's first-person testimony is re-owned rather than attributed: 'It has for me. I have not lived and done all the good for which I longed' becomes 'At least for me, it's been very true this week that I haven't done all the good that I long to do' (0:56:23).

Statements are converted into congregational participation: Begg's 'take this and take it to yourself. God is for us' becomes 'Take this and take it for yourself and say this to yourself first. God is for me. Now, let's say it out loud. God is for me' (1:05:13); and the outline itself is turned into a call-and-response, 'Say that with me' (0:44:15).

Begg's illustrations are swapped for American pop-culture equivalents in the same rhetorical slots: Toplady's hymns become Pogo and Johnny Cochran; the dandelion becomes the bicycle pedals; the plain 'sleep like a baby' becomes a John McCain talk-show joke.
Begg's declarative assertions become rhetorical questions to the room: 'Who can bring a charge against you?' becomes 'Guess who it is? It's you' (0:57:44) and 'Are you guilty before God?' (1:04:13).

Precision is loosened, sometimes into error: Begg's careful 'the experience of all real Christians everywhere and at all times' is reassigned by FBC to a verse — 'Paul is affirming this in 1 Thessalonians 5:4' (0:52:45) — a citation that does not say that.
rating_rationale: This is not influence; it is a re-preached manuscript. The FBC sermon follows Begg's 'The Faithfulness of God' from its opening exegetical claim (the hapax 'blameless at his coming' and the Thessalonican tombstones) through its pivot to Romans 8 ('how can we be sure of this? Turn to this great chapter'), its Romans 1-5 recap, its Westminster Confession citation, its Packer list, its four Romans 8 sub-points, and out through its final take-home line ('carve that into your mind ... one thing I know for sure, God is for me') — the same ideas, in the same order, in very largely the same words. The machine found 31% of the sermon window in near-verbatim alignment, and that undercounts, because the un-aligned stretches are mostly FBC illustrations inserted into slots that Begg's outline created. Every secondary source the preacher cites (Zinzendorf, Phillips, the Westminster Confession, 'Jer'/Packer) is a source Begg cites at the same moment, and several borrowings carry transmission damage — a dropped negation, a dangling 'which he then abandons', a stumble over 'the great four-word statements' — which shows recitation rather than composition. Begg and Truth For Life are never named, and no borrowing signal of any kind is given; Begg's own 'that's been true this week ... for me' confession is delivered as the preacher's own. I withhold a 10 only because the delivery is genuinely re-voiced, roughly a third of the airtime is his own illustration and local application, and a handful of small theological touches ('there's a difference between being innocent and blameless') are his.

Because if you understood me to the depth that He does, you'd never talk to me again. ... Don't allow the devil to drag you back to the garbage cans of sins that have been settled at Calvary long ago. ... Hide in the faithfulness of God."

FBC (1:13:33): "If God is for me, carve that into your mind today. ... One thing I know for sure, God is for you and he's for me." | BEGG: "carve it into your recollection as you begin tomorrow morning ... say this to yourself, well I know one thing for sure, God is for me."
caveats: The FBC text is YouTube auto-captioning of a live room with a hot mic, and the Begg text is Whisper ASR of an audio archive; both mangle proper nouns. 'Count Ludri von Zeninsorf' is Zinzendorf, 'holocaros'/'holoclerus' is holokleros, 'Jer put it so eloquently' is almost certainly 'J.I. Packer put it so eloquently' (Begg's transcript renders the same name 'Packard'), and 'Jay Lyn' is Jay Leno. Word-level identity scores should therefore be read as floors, not ceilings.

1 Thessalonians 5:23-24 is the preaching text for both men, so every occurrence of 'the one who calls you is faithful and he will do it' (alignment regions 1-3, 9-11) is Scripture read aloud and is NOT evidence of borrowing. The same applies to the shared quotations of Philippians 1:6, 1 John 3:2, Romans 4:23-25, 7:24, 8:1, 8:31-35. The machine's small overlap with volume2/02-sexualpuritypartone.txt is entirely of this kind: that sermon quotes 1 Thess 5:23-24 in full while looking ahead to chapter 5, and nothing in the FBC sermon matches its surrounding commentary. It should be disregarded.

The machine's Scripture labels on several regions are wrong and were re-judged by hand: region 24 ('what are we going to say to it, what are we going to do') is tagged 'Exodus 16' but is Begg's rhetoric, and regions 1-3/9-11 are tagged 'Daniel 11' but are 1 Thessalonians 5:24.

Some overlapping language is genuine evangelical stock and carries little weight on its own: 'filthy rags', 'fiery darts of the evil one', 'we are under construction', 'no condemnation ... no separation' as a summary of Romans 8. These were not counted as findings; the case rests on the exegetical claims, the secondary citations, the first-person confession, the Packer list, the four-point structure and the peroration.

The two men have different sermon economies: Begg's is an evening exposition ending in Toplady and 'Take my life and let it be'; FBC's is a Sunday-morning message with congregational response, a local-event tie-in and a pastoral prayer. The re-voicing is real. The judgement here is about the substance and its order, not about delivery.

I checked the other eighteen Begg transcripts in source_transcripts/ for the FBC sermon's non-aligned material. Nothing else matched: 'garbage cans of sin' also appears in volume3/09-sanctification.txt, but that is Begg reusing his own phrase, and the FBC context (Romans 8:33, accusation) matches volume3/10 rather than 09. Pogo, Walt Kelly, Johnny Cochran, Robert Shapiro, John McCain, the bicycle pedals, the rainbow photograph and 'let's get ready to rumble' appear nowhere in the Begg corpus and should be treated as the FBC preacher's own.
